jobs.title: Twikey: Senior Java Developer
jobs.description:
Headquarters: Ghent - Belgium
URL: https://www.twikey.com/jobs

Are you a driven back-end developer who doesn't wait for instructions, but is already thinking two steps ahead? Who experiments with new technologies and smart solutions alongside the job? Then we want to talk to you.

Straight forward but clear: Twikey isn't looking for someone to just execute. We're looking for someone who thinks, does and keeps going when the going gets tough.

Because fintech is evolving at breakneck speed. That calls for real ownership and for someone who can dive deep on the technical side to keep innovating and improving our platform. You get plenty in return, such as the freedom and responsibility to deliver your own projects. Thanks in part to our organisational structure, you can shape your ideas in the short term and see the results of your hard work quickly.

Driven by your passion for building scalable, performant and secure back-end systems, you continuously raise the bar for your own skills and for our product.

As a member of our development team you work closely with our CTO, 3 fellow developers and 2 testers on the core of our software application. A small, strong team in which you take on a role with real impact on the future of our product.

  • You focus on developing and improving the back-end of our platform, optimising the architecture and data processing while keeping the security and stability of our system in mind. This lets you put your technical skills to full use and come up with innovative solutions.
  • With your expertise you'll make valuable suggestions and streamline processes for all our stakeholders, so we can work more efficiently and achieve better results.
  • You provide technical support on integration projects with software houses, banks and large companies, solving complex technical problems. That gives you the chance to work on challenging projects and to get in touch with a wide range of technologies and industries.

Once you know our product inside out, there are plenty of challenging projects for you to help build.

What are we looking for in you?

  • You are driven, curious and enterprising. Not only in your job, but outside of it too. You have a pro-active attitude and are always a few steps ahead: you spot opportunities, grab them and get to work.
  • Technical challenges? You take them on, not because you have to, but because you want to learn. You're a self-starter and quickly get to grips with new technologies, languages or frameworks.
  • You understand that a good product is never "finished". You draw energy from that mix of creating and fine-tuning. You think along, question things and keep building new solutions.
  • You have experience using AI tools to build integrations. You're actively exploring how AI can contribute to smarter user experiences and more efficient software development. Experience with data analytics is an asset.
  • You therefore attach a lot of importance to the security, stability and reliability of a system and know what it takes to get there. You work in a structured, meticulous way and write code that is clean, reusable and easy to test.
  • You have demonstrable experience with Java, Go and the Spring framework. Experience with API integrations, web services, Linux or other relevant areas is a plus.
  • You have a deep understanding of databases. You don't just know how to use them, you know how they work. You have an opinion on structured, high-quality code, architecture and back-end technologies.
  • You have a very good command of English, for smooth collaboration with all colleagues and stakeholders. Dutch is an asset.
  • You are based in a time zone within one hour of CET, so your working day overlaps with the team's for the daily stand-ups and close day-to-day collaboration.
  • You can work independently and enjoy a small team where switching gears quickly, collaboration and knowledge sharing are central.

Twikey offers you:

  • An environment where challenge, innovation and autonomy come first.
  • The room to experiment, to challenge and to improve. And we expect you to really take that room.
  • An ideal setting if you want to grow fast and healthily, both technically and personally. Training, ownership, taking on new or additional roles based on your talents and interests, ... a lot is possible here, and you're at the wheel!
  • A complementary team of more than 35 colleagues who move forward together in a respectful and open atmosphere.
  • A motivating workplace with plenty of knowledge and expertise, shared both formally during the daily stand-ups and the weekly Friday call, and informally at the coffee machine.
  • Appreciation, openness and critical dialogue. Our Friction Hunter Trophy is an example: every month we celebrate the colleague who made the biggest difference for customers, teammates or internally. Your impact gets noticed!
  • A modern workplace with different zones (conference, connect, co-work, concentrate) in a recently built, industrial-style office building. Easy to reach by car, by bike and by public transport on the edge of Ghent, right next to the KBC tower.
  • A salary package tailored to your experience and skills, with plenty of extra-legal benefits, a collective bonus system and a cafeteria plan to convert your 13th month as you choose.
  • The chance to work in an innovative Belgian fintech scale-up that is active in several countries, in a sector that is growing fast!

A job ad doesn't tell you everything. Our colleagues tell you here what it's really like to work at Twikey.

To apply: https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/twikey-senior-java-developer

  • Interact with a wide variety of colleagues, customers, and stakeholders at all levels with respect, courtesy, and professionalism.

sa.global is looking for a driven and talented Business Development Manager with proven sales expertise to join our dynamic team. This role requires building and maintaining successful relationships with both prospects and existing clients.

  • Leverage global marketing campaigns and drive local demand generation activities that attract prospective and existing clients to build a robust sales pipeline.
  • Conduct regular account planning and business development sessions with Microsoft contacts to jointly target opportunities, develop offerings, and secure funding.

  • Extensive software sales experience with a proven track record of developing new client relationships and closing sales.
  • A demonstrated track-record of consistently meeting or exceeding annual quotas and performance targets, in B2B sales of Dynamics 365 or similar ERP products.
  • Proven success managing complex, long-cycle sales campaigns in a fast-paced, consultative, and competitive market.
  • Commercially minded, with the ability to understand and address business challenges.
  • Demonstrated success in initiating, negotiating, winning, and growing strategic partnerships.

  • Excellent English communication skills.
  • Excellent presentation and public speaking skills, with the ability to present confidently at senior levels.
  • Excellent relationship-building and management skills, with experience engaging with C-suite executives.

About the Job

At HYROS, we help businesses understand exactly where their customers and revenue come from through advanced ad tracking and attribution.

We're looking for an experienced Customer Success Manager with 5+ years of experience to own high-touch onboarding and customer success for key customers.

This is not a purely relationship-focused CSM role. Onboarding at HYROS has a strong technical component. You'll need to understand how a customer's marketing and sales ecosystem works, help them connect the right platforms, troubleshoot setup issues, and make sure their tracking is working correctly.

Your goal is clear: help customers get set up correctly, reach value fast, trust their data, and use HYROS to make better business decisions.

This is a high-ownership role. You'll lead customer relationships, identify risks early, solve problems proactively, and be accountable for successful onboarding, adoption, and retention.

What You'll Own & What Success Looks Like

As a Customer Success Manager at HYROS, you'll be responsible for guiding customers through onboarding, helping them get real value from their data, and building strong relationships that support long-term retention.

Your performance will be measured across four key areas:

  1. Customer Retention: The percentage of customers you successfully retain within your assigned portfolio.

  2. Customer Portfolio: The number of customers you manage while maintaining a high standard of service and engagement.

  3. Onboarding & Activation: How effectively you guide customers through technical implementation, complete their setup, and help them start using HYROS.

  4. Customer Satisfaction: The quality of your customer relationships, feedback, and ability to resolve issues proactively.

What Success in This Role Looks Like

First 30 Days — Learning & First Customers

  • Understand HYROS, our onboarding playbooks, internal processes, and customer journey.

  • Become familiar with our tracking technology, integrations, and common implementation challenges.

  • Understand how platforms like Meta Ads, Google Ads, Shopify, CRMs, and payment processors connect with HYROS.

  • Start hosting onboarding calls and guiding your first customers through their setup.

  • Learn how to troubleshoot common tracking, integration, and data validation issues.

First 60 Days — Building Independence

  • Confidently lead onboarding calls and guide customers through technical implementations.

  • Become comfortable helping customers install tracking scripts, configure integrations, validate events, and troubleshoot setup issues.

  • Independently manage your first customer portfolio and keep onboarding progress on track.

  • Identify potential setup or engagement risks early and take action before they become bigger problems.

  • Develop a strong understanding of how customers use HYROS data to improve their advertising decisions.

First 90 Days — Full Ownership

  • Take full ownership of your assigned customers, from onboarding through activation and ongoing adoption.

  • Independently handle most common technical onboarding challenges, knowing when deeper technical support is needed.

  • Run effective customer training sessions and explain complex tracking concepts in a simple, practical way.

  • Help customers understand their attribution data and turn it into actionable business decisions.

  • Proactively manage customer engagement, satisfaction, and retention risks.

  • Maintain strong relationships and consistently positive customer feedback.

First 180 Days — Consistent Performance

  • Independently manage a growing customer portfolio while maintaining a high standard of customer service.

  • Consistently deliver successful onboarding, strong adoption, and positive customer retention.

  • Become a trusted advisor who helps customers make better marketing and business decisions using HYROS.

  • Demonstrate strong technical confidence across common integrations, tracking setups, and troubleshooting scenarios.

  • Identify opportunities to improve onboarding efficiency, customer experience, and retention.

  • Contribute to improving internal playbooks, processes, and best practices.

What We're Looking For

  • 5+ years of Customer Success experience, ideally in SaaS.

  • Experience managing high-touch or strategic customers.

  • Strong understanding of customer onboarding, adoption, and retention.

  • Comfort working in technical customer environments. You don't need to be a developer, but technical implementations shouldn't intimidate you.

  • Hands-on familiarity with platforms such as Meta Ads, Google Ads, Shopify, or similar marketing and e-commerce platforms.

  • Comfortable understanding how websites, funnels, tracking scripts, integrations, pixels/events, and customer data connect at a practical level.

  • Able to troubleshoot logically, identify where a setup may be breaking, and clearly explain the solution to a customer.

  • Excellent communication skills and the ability to make complex or technical topics simple.

  • Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to work independently.

  • Comfortable using data and customer signals to prioritize and take action.

  • A proactive, ownership-driven mindset. You don't wait for problems to become escalations.

Big Plus

  • Experience with marketing analytics, paid advertising, ad tracking, attribution, conversion tracking, e-commerce, or technical SaaS products.

  • Experience with platforms and tools such as Meta Ads, Google Ads, Shopify, HubSpot, Intercom, or ChurnZero.

  • Basic familiarity with concepts such as tracking scripts, pixels, events, domains, redirects, webhooks, APIs, UTMs, and CRM integrations.

  • Previous experience managing customer portfolios with a strong focus on retention, customer satisfaction, and long-term adoption.

Why HYROS?

You'll have real ownership over a critical part of the customer journey and a direct impact on onboarding, adoption, retention, and customer success.

You'll work at the intersection of Customer Success, marketing, data, and technology, helping businesses not only implement HYROS correctly but actually use it to make better decisions.

This is an opportunity to work directly with customers, solve meaningful technical challenges, and see the impact of your work on their businesses.

If you're an experienced CSM who enjoys building customer relationships but is also comfortable getting hands-on with technical setups, troubleshooting problems, and understanding how marketing technology works, we'd like to hear from you.

jobs.title: Vercel: Security Software Engineer, IAM
jobs.description:
Headquarters: Remote - United States

About Vercel:

Vercel is the agentic infrastructure company, freeing people and agents to ship what's next. For more than a decade we've helped builders move from idea to production with speed, security, and exceptional developer experience.

Now we're scaling our products for both agents and people to ship and run software, built in the open and trusted by OpenAI, PayPal, Ramp, Supreme, and millions of developers worldwide.

About the Role:

Traditional IAM teams operate as an approval queue: a request comes in, someone reviews it, grants it, and (hopefully) remembers to revoke it. Access reviews become quarterly spreadsheet exercises, audit evidence is assembled by hand, and the central team becomes the bottleneck for every decision. That model doesn't scale past a certain point, and Vercel is past it. Adding more approvers doesn't close the gap. Building the system that makes access self-serve, time-bound, and provable does.

This role is about building that system. Identity at Vercel should work like the rest of our infrastructure: defined as code, reviewed in pull requests, deployed through CI, and observable in production. You'll own that transformation end to end: migrating Okta and all related IAM configuration fully behind Terraform, and building the self-serve access platform (including just-in-time access) that lets team and system owners define, request, and time-bound their own access instead of routing every decision through a central team. Provisioning, deprovisioning, and access reviews become workflows the system runs, with the audit evidence for SOC 2 and similar generated as a byproduct rather than a manual scramble.

You'll also own the harder connective work: corporate IAM (employee identity, SaaS access, devices) and production IAM (service accounts, infrastructure permissions, on-call and prod access) usually live in separate silos with separate tools and separate evidence trails. You'll build them as one identity plane.

And identity itself is changing shape. As agents increasingly act on behalf of users and systems, the old model of "one human, one identity" doesn't hold, and there's real debate about how to solve it: carry the human's identity through every hop the agent makes, or give the agent its own scoped identity that never impersonates the user. We don't have a fixed answer yet. We want someone who wants to be in the room helping us decide and then build it.

Because of this, we're optimizing for someone who wants to build identity infrastructure as software, not administer identity products. A software engineer who's gone deep on identity, or an IAM engineer with a strong engineering background, is exactly who we're looking for.

You'll work closely with Security Leadership, located remotely within the United States. If you're based within commuting distance of our SF or NY offices, the role includes in-office anchor days on Monday, Tuesday, and Friday.

What You Will Do:

  • Own the full IAM strategy for corporate, production, and product environments end to end, and own the bridge between corp IAM and product/prod IAM rather than treating them as separate problems
  • Migrate Okta and all related IAM configuration to Terraform, so every identity change is reviewed, tested, and versioned like the rest of our infrastructure, driving infrastructure-as-code adoption and leveling up engineering teams in its use
  • Build self-serve access governance tooling, including JIT (just-in-time) access: design and ship the framework that lets team and system owners define, request, and time-bound their own access, rather than security being a bottleneck for every request
  • Own provisioning, deprovisioning, and access review workflows, built so the evidence trail generates itself and internal and external audits (SOC 2 and similar) are fast, not a manual scramble
  • Work closely with the Accounts team, the engineers who build IAM into Vercel's own product (team and project roles, enterprise SSO, SCIM, API tokens), and find where that world and ours should connect
  • Design and enforce least-privilege access controls across cloud, SaaS, and production infrastructure, partnering with platform and engineering teams to embed IAM early in design rather than bolting it on after
  • Help define what identity and access should look like as agents, not just people, request and hold access at Vercel, and build the first versions of it

About You:

  • 7+ years of experience in identity, access management, or platform security engineering
  • Experience building internal tools or self-service platforms, not just administering existing ones. You'd rather build the framework that lets other teams manage their own access than be the sole approver for every request
  • Proficient in a production language like TypeScript/Node.js, Go, or Python, comfortable designing and consuming REST APIs, and able to ship and operate reliable services. The access platform you'll build is a production system, not a configuration
  • Proficient in Terraform and committed to managing IAM infrastructure as code, ideally with experience migrating existing systems into it
  • Hands-on with identity protocols (OAuth2, OIDC, SAML, SCIM) at the implementation level, not just configuration, including the failure modes: token replay, deprovisioned users retaining access, sync drift between identity providers and downstream systems
  • Experience designing IAM at scale across both corporate (Okta or equivalent: SSO, MFA, lifecycle management, API-driven automation) and production (AWS or GCP IAM: service accounts, roles, workload identity federation) environments
  • A systems thinker who defaults to "why does this class of access request exist" and "how does this scale to the next thousand employees and ten thousand agents," not just resolving the request in front of you
  • Strong collaborator who can drive alignment across Engineering, IT, Compliance, and Security teams
  • Comfortable operating with autonomy and owning decisions in a fast-moving environment

Bonus If You Have

  • Have led a Terraform migration for IAM or identity infrastructure at scale.
  • Have designed or built JIT access systems or an access governance/request platform at a previous company.
  • Have built or managed MDM/MAM tooling (Jamf, Intune, or equivalent) and device-trust integrations with identity.
  • Understand how Vercel's own products handle IAM (team and project roles, enterprise SSO, API tokens) and are excited to partner with the Accounts team to bring internal and product-facing identity closer together.
  • Have a point of view on agent identity (delegation, scoped credentials, impersonation boundaries) and want to help invent the architecture rather than apply an existing playbook.
  • Have experience at a developer tools, infrastructure, or SaaS company.
  • Hold certifications such as Okta Certified Professional/Administrator, AWS Security Specialty, or CISSP. These demonstrate depth, though they're not required.

Compensation & Benefits:

jobs.title: Abnormal: Director of Security Engineering
jobs.description:
Headquarters: Remote - USA

About the Role

Abnormal AI protects organizations from the most sophisticated email and collaboration attacks using behavioral AI. Security is not a bolt-on at Abnormal; it is core to the product we sell and the trust our customers place in us. Our security organization operates a commercial cloud environment and a separate FedRAMP-authorized environment, and we are pursuing increasingly rigorous federal authorizations as we grow.

We are hiring a Director of Security reporting to the CISO and leading the Security Engineering organization. You will build and scale high-performing security teams, own major security programs end to end, and operate autonomously in the CISO's absence, including representing security to executive leadership, customers, and auditors.

This is a role for a deeply technical leader with a software engineering background who has grown into people leadership. You have built security teams from the ground up, you write and review code and architecture when it matters, and you believe the best security organizations earn their influence through partnership rather than policy enforcement.

Our Security Philosophy

We run security the way the best engineering-led companies do:

  • Security reduces toil. Our job is to make the rest of the company faster and safer at the same time. If a control adds friction without reducing risk, it is a defect.
  • Paved paths, safe by default. We invest in guardrails, golden paths, and secure-by-default infrastructure so the easy choice is the secure choice. We prefer preventing classes of problems over chasing individual findings.
  • Partnership over gatekeeping. Security succeeds only through deep collaboration with engineering, IT, and business teams. We embed with builders, we ship alongside them, and we take on their constraints as our own.
  • Engineering-grade rigor. We treat security problems as engineering problems: automated, measurable, code-reviewed, and continuously improved.

If the security cultures that value freedom and responsibility, context over control, and guardrails over gates resonate with you, you will feel at home here.

What You Will Do

  • Serve as deputy to the CISO: act with full authority in the CISO's absence and represent the security organization to executives, customers, and regulators.
  • Lead, coach, and grow managers and senior engineers across Security Engineering and Security Operations.
  • Own the security engineering roadmap: cloud security architecture (AWS-first), detection and response, identity, vulnerability management, and secure-by-default platform investments.
  • Drive cross-functional programs with Engineering, IT, and Product, from AI security governance to data perimeter controls to federal compliance initiatives.
  • Set and defend engineering standards for the security organization: everything as code, automated where possible, measured against outcomes rather than activity.
  • Build hiring pipelines and raise the bar on every hire; own performance management, promotion cases, and succession planning within your teams.
  • Translate technical risk into business terms for the executive team and board, and translate business priorities into a coherent security strategy.

Must Haves

  • 10+ years in security or software engineering, including 4+ years managing security teams, ideally including managers of managers or equivalent scope.
  • A genuine software engineering background: you have shipped production software, and you evaluate security solutions the way an engineer would.
  • A proven record of building and scaling high-performing security teams, with alumni who would work for you again.
  • Deep technical fluency in cloud-native environments: AWS organizations and multi-account governance, Kubernetes, identity and access, detection engineering, and modern SDLC security.
  • Demonstrated cross-functional leadership: you have earned the trust of engineering leaders and shipped security outcomes through their teams, not around them.
  • Strong written communication: you produce decision-ready documents and can drive alignment asynchronously.
  • Executive presence: comfortable presenting to C-level leadership, customers, and auditors without preparation from the CISO.

Strong Signals

  • You are currently a security engineering manager or senior manager at a fintech, high-growth startup, or forward-leaning enterprise, and you are ready for broader scope.
  • You have built paved-path or secure-by-default platforms that measurably reduced both risk and developer friction.
  • Experience with compliance-driven environments (FedRAMP, SOC 2, ISO 27001) without letting compliance define the security program.
  • Experience securing AI/ML systems or governing AI adoption at scale.
  • You have operated in environments where security headcount was scarce and automation was the only way to scale.

Why This Role

You will inherit strong teams, an executive staff that treats security as a first-class function, and a CISO who wants a true partner rather than a lieutenant. The scope is broad, the autonomy is real, and the ceiling on this role is defined by what you take on.

jobs.title: Vercel: Design Engineer
jobs.description:
Headquarters: Remote - United States

About Vercel:

Vercel is the agentic infrastructure company, freeing people and agents to ship what's next. For more than a decade we've helped builders move from idea to production with speed, security, and exceptional developer experience.

Now we're scaling our products for both agents and people to ship and run software, built in the open and trusted by OpenAI, PayPal, Ramp, Supreme, and millions of developers worldwide.

About the Role:

AI Gateway gives developers one place to connect applications and agents to hundreds of models with one API key. It handles provider routing and fallbacks, unifies billing and observability, and lets teams manage spend and security controls across production AI workloads.

Designing this well is a systems problem. A developer should be able to choose the right model, make and verify a first request, diagnose a failed request, and configure routing, budgets, credentials, and security controls without losing sight of the application they are trying to build. The right interface might be in the dashboard, on the public model catalog, in the CLI, in an API response, or in code.

You will be the Design Engineer for AI Gateway, owning product design and frontend implementation across those surfaces. You will work with customers, a Product Manager, and engineers to understand the problem, explore solutions, build the production experience, ship it, and learn from what happens after launch.

AI Gateway is live, the model ecosystem changes every week, and the team can move from an observed problem to production quickly. This is a rare chance to use your product judgment, design craft, and code to shape a developer product and ship the experience yourself.

You will be the design owner embedded with a Product Manager and a dedicated engineering team. You will also have the Product Design team around you for critique, collaboration, and support. AI Gateway will be your main product area, with room to pursue design-led improvements across Vercel. You will report to the Design Team.

If you’re based within a pre-determined commuting distance of one of our offices (SF, NY, London, or Berlin), the role includes in-office anchor days on Monday, Tuesday, and Friday. If you're located beyond that distance, the role is fully remote. For location-specific details, please connect with our recruiting team.

What You Will Do:

  • Own product design and frontend implementation for meaningful parts of the journey from discovering a model to making a first successful request and operating AI in production.
  • Design and build production experiences across the website, dashboard, CLI, and APIs, choosing the right medium for each problem.
  • Make models, providers, credentials, routing, budgets, logs, performance, privacy, and governance understandable, then create patterns that extend across new providers, modalities, and workloads.
  • Talk directly with customers and use product data to understand problems, define success, make tradeoffs, and improve what ships.
  • Own quality after launch, including visual and interaction craft, accessibility, performance, resilience, instrumentation, and edge cases.
  • Use coding agents to explore and implement ideas quickly, while testing, debugging, and taking responsibility for what ships.

About You:

  • Your work shows what you personally identified, designed, built, shipped, and learned after launch.
  • You build production-quality web applications with React and TypeScript and can contribute confidently in a large, existing codebase.
  • You bring strong visual and interaction craft and have made technical or data-rich products understandable without removing the control advanced users need.
  • You can move between graphical interfaces, CLI workflows, API behavior, and implementation details, treating accessibility, performance, failure recovery, and instrumentation as part of the design.
  • You use customer research and product data to make decisions, communicate your reasoning clearly, challenge ideas constructively, and change direction when the evidence changes.
  • You use coding agents in your daily work, but you can explain, test, debug, and take responsibility for the code they help produce.

There is no required path into this role. You may come from product design, frontend engineering, creative development, or a career that does not fit a standard title. We care about the quality of what you have shipped and the judgment behind it.

jobs.title: Calm.com: Senior Product Designer
jobs.description:
Headquarters: Remote, United States

About Calm

Calm is the leading mental health brand on a mission to make the world happier and healthier. Known for its flagship consumer app—ranked #1 in its category with over 180 million downloads and availability in ten languages across 190 countries—Calm helps people sleep better, stress less, and live more mindfully through content and tools from experts and beloved celebrity voices. Building on this foundation, Calm has created a broader portfolio including evidence-based solutions like Calm Health, offered through employers, health plans and providers, designed to expand access to mental health and sleep support, boost benefits engagement, and drive positive health outcomes. Today, Calm supports more than 3,500 organizations and reaches over 42 million covered lives through Calm Health. Calm has been recognized as a TIME100 Most Influential Company and one of Fast Company’s Brands That Matter. Learn more at calm.com.

What We Do

At Calm we believe in making relaxation, better sleep, and mindfulness accessible to the entire world, and we hope you will help us achieve our mission. The Product & Design team is responsible for delivering Calm to our customers, ensuring that it is easy to use, supports their goals, and maintains a high level of quality across web, iOS, Android platforms.

As a Senior Product Designer on our Consumer team, you'll shape experiences used by tens of millions of people to sleep better, stress less, and live more mindfully. People often reach for Calm in their most vulnerable moments, so the craft of what we make (how it looks, moves, and feels) matters enormously. 

This is a builder's role in the truest sense: you'll use AI and modern prototyping tools to move from insight to interactive prototype to shipped experience, not as a shortcut on quality, but to spend less time producing and more time on the judgment and detail that make an experience great. When anyone can generate a hundred screens in an afternoon, taste and judgment are the differentiators! 

The heart of this role is balancing velocity and craft in service of making our users healthier and happier, and building intuitive, engaging and impactful experiences that drive acquisition, engagement and retention.  You'll partner closely with Product Management, Engineering, Data Science, and Marketing, and set the standard for craft across iOS, Android, and web.  You will be a thought leader in design, helping to establish best practices and setting the bar for exceptional product design at Calm.

What You’ll Do

  • Own end-to-end product design initiatives that cover the whole product experience (visual, interaction, motion, brand integration), to create thoughtful, high-quality user-centered mobile experiences.
  • Prototype quickly in Figma and with AI and low-code tools like Replit, Lovable, and Claude, so you can get real, testable ideas in front of people early.
  • Present your design work clearly and persuasively to cross-functional stakeholders (including senior leadership), give and take feedback well, anchoring your rationale to both user needs and business goals.
  • Maintain strong attention to detail and collaboration through engineering implementation (build and QA) and post launch-iterations, to ensure high-quality execution.
  • Use data and drive research to inform the experiences you build, and leverage performance insights to evolve your approach.
  • Champion system-level thinking (improving how the team works and evolving Calm's design system) so the whole team works faster and smarter.
  • Balance multiple projects in a fast-paced environment while maintaining high standards of execution. 

Who You Are

  • Experienced Product Designer: 7+ years of experience in UX and UI design with 5+ within consumer mobile and web applications.
  • AI-native and tooling-fluent: Highly proficient in Figma for design, and already using AI and low-code tools (Replit, Lovable, Claude) to prototype and move fast, with the judgment to know when the output is good enough and when it isn't.
  • Technical agility: Comfortable shipping small code changes without engineering support, bridging the gap between design and engineering by personally shipping copy and UI polish directly.
  • A builder: Biased toward shipping and iterating over perfect plans. You'd rather put a working prototype in front of people than write a doc about one.
  • Data- and research-informed: You fold both qualitative and quantitative insight into your design decisions, and you measure whether the work landed.
  • A strong collaborator: A low-ego, trusted partner to Product, Research, and Engineering who makes the people around them better and helps sharpen how the team works.
  • High craft standards: A strong advocate for accessibility, consistency, visual storytelling, brand integration, and motion design to create engaging user experiences, while still maintaining velocity.
  • A clear communicator: You present your thinking persuasively to stakeholders and senior leadership, give and take feedback well, and champion an experience while staying open to being wrong.

Nice to Haves

  • Experience with conversational or AI-native UX.
  • Experience working at multiple organizations, ideally including time at a consumer product in a fast-paced startup environment.
  • A strong portfolio demonstrating your ability to design and ship beautiful, functional, and user-friendly experiences.
  • Comfort shipping small copy and UI changes directly in code, without engineering support.
  • A passion for Calm's mission and a point of view on how digital products can support mental health.

Minimum Requirements

  • 7+ years in UX/UI design with 5+ within consumer mobile (and web) applications.
  • Proven experience driving user testing and research.
  • Strong foundation in interaction design, visual design, and usability best practices.
  • Experience designing and shipping mobile applications at scale.
  • Hands-on proficiency in Figma and modern AI/prototyping tools.
  • Ability to work independently while contributing to a larger design vision and strategy.

Calm uses a geographic pay model that determines salaries based on the location where an employee lives. For this position, the base pay ranges across Calm’s pay tiers is as follows: $168,000 - $245,000. The base pay range represents the low and high end of Calm’s salary range for this position. Not all candidates will be eligible for the upper end of the salary range. Exact salary will ultimately depend on multiple factors, which include the successful candidate's geographic location, skills, experience and other qualifications. Calm uses employee zip code to determine which pay range applies. This role is also eligible for equity + comprehensive benefits + 401k + flexible time off.

Calm may incorporate artificial intelligence technology to support the application review process, but rest assured that human reviewers are involved in all stages of the hiring process.

Calm is committed to providing reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities, including disabled veterans. If you require a reasonable accommodation to complete any part of the application or interview process, please contact Calm’s Recruiting team at recruitingaccommodations@calm.com. All accommodation requests will be handled confidentially and assessed on a case-by-case basis.

We believe that mental health is health, and every person should be considered in the discussion. That’s why we’re proud to be an equal opportunity workplace, committed to providing equal employment opportunities to all applicants and employees regardless of race, color, religion, national origin, age, sex, marital status, ancestry, physical or mental disability, medical condition, genetic information, military or veteran status, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state or local law.

Calm is deeply committed to diversity, equity and inclusion. We strive to create a mindful and respectful environment where everyone can bring their authentic self to work, and experience a culture that is free of harassment, racism, and discrimination.

Employment offers are contingent upon the successful completion of a background check. Roles which require access to certain types of information may also require the successful completion of a drug screening.

jobs.title: Ace Ventures: Executive Personal Assistant to the Founder (Remote, UAE or Europe)
jobs.description:
Headquarters: Dubai, United Arab Emirates
URL: https://aceventures.ai/

Location: Remote, based in the UAE or Europe. Engagement: full-time independent contractor (own visa and invoicing setup required).

About the role

You will be the right hand to a Dubai-based founder who runs a group of companies in performance marketing and consumer brands and splits his time between Dubai and Europe. Your job is to take every administrative task off his plate, business and personal, so his time goes to decisions and deals rather than logistics.

We are looking for an A player. This is a fast-moving environment with high expectations: priorities change daily, decisions are made quickly, and the standard is that things get done properly the first time. You need to be driven, want to work hard, and take pride in running a tight operation for someone who moves fast.

This is a hands-on, high-trust role. You will handle calendars, travel, bookings, paperwork, payments, vendors and follow-ups across several companies and several countries. You should be the kind of person who closes loops without being chased and notices problems before they land on his desk.

What you will own

Business administration

  • Manage calendar and inbox: triage, prioritise, draft replies, schedule and reschedule across time zones
  • Prepare, chase and file documents: contracts for signature, invoices, KYC and compliance requests from banks and partners, company renewals (trade licences, visas, insurance)
  • Coordinate with accountants, lawyers, banks and agencies; track deadlines so nothing lapses
  • Keep shared drives, access lists and company records organised and current
  • Take notes in meetings when asked, track action items and follow up with the people responsible

Travel and bookings

  • Plan and book flights, hotels, villas, ground transport and restaurants, often on short notice and with changes mid-trip
  • Manage loyalty programmes, entry requirements, visas and travel documents
  • Coordinate pet travel logistics when required

Personal administration

  • Handle personal bills, subscriptions, insurance, vehicles and property matters in Dubai and Europe
  • Manage household staff and service providers (cleaning, maintenance, vets, groomers, trainers)
  • Research and arrange appointments, gifts, events and reservations
  • Run errands remotely: returns, deliveries, renewals, forms

What success looks like

  • By day 30: You own the calendar and inbox end to end, know every company entity, bank and key contact, and have a live tracker of renewals and deadlines.
  • By day 60: You have handled at least one full international trip solo, including changes mid-trip, and taken over all personal bills and subscriptions.
  • By day 90: The founder is not touching admin. You flag issues before they become urgent and propose fixes rather than questions.

What we are looking for

  • 3+ years as an executive assistant, personal assistant or chief of staff to a founder, senior executive or private individual
  • Based in the UAE or Europe, already holding the right to live and work there, and able to invoice as a freelancer or through your own company
  • Fluent written and spoken English is required; any additional languages are a plus
  • Proven experience booking complex international travel and handling last-minute changes calmly
  • Comfortable with numbers and paperwork: expenses, invoices, bank forms, compliance requests
  • Strong with Google Workspace, WhatsApp, Slack, Notion or similar, and quick to learn new tools
  • Skilled with AI tools such as Claude and ChatGPT: you use them daily for drafting, research, summarising and structuring work, not as an occasional experiment
  • Track record of automating your own repetitive tasks (for example with Zapier, Make, n8n, spreadsheet scripts or AI agents) without being asked to
  • Discreet by default; you will see sensitive financial, legal and personal information
  • Self-directed: works from a list, chases without reminders, confirms when something is done
  • Calm under pressure, allergic to loose ends, direct in communication, and comfortable working mostly alone with a founder who moves fast and changes plans often

This role is not for you if

You need a fixed 9 to 5 with no interruptions, you prefer to wait for instructions rather than propose a plan, or you are uncomfortable handling someone else's money, documents and personal life with total discretion.

Tools we use

Google Workspace (Gmail, Calendar, Drive), WhatsApp and Slack for daily communication, Notion for tasks and documentation, Claude for drafting, research and workflow automation, and standard travel and booking platforms. Experience with UAE government portals (GDRFA, DED, Dubai Now) and European banking is useful but not required.

Working hours and availability

  • Core hours: 09:00 to 18:00 Gulf Standard Time (UTC+4), Monday to Friday
  • When the founder is in Europe, core hours shift to Central European Time
  • Reachable for urgent travel or booking issues outside core hours and on weekends; this is balanced with flexible time off during quiet periods
  • Occasional in-person time in Dubai or Europe (a few days per quarter) is a plus, not a requirement

Confidentiality and trust

You will have access to passports, payment cards, company accounts and private correspondence. The engagement is conditional on a signed NDA, reference checks and a background check. Access is granted step by step during the probation period.

Compensation and terms

  • Fee: EUR 3,500 to 5,000 per month (or AED equivalent), depending on location and experience, invoiced monthly
  • Performance bonus: up to EUR 2,000 per month on top of the fee, assessed monthly against agreed targets (deadlines met, zero missed renewals or bookings, response times, issues caught before they became urgent)
  • Engagement: independent contractor. You must already hold the legal right to live and work where you are based and be set up to invoice (freelance permit, sole trader, autónomo or your own company). No visa sponsorship is provided.
  • Software and travel costs covered when in-person time is needed
  • Three-month probation period

How to apply

Apply with your CV, your earliest start date, and short written answers (a few sentences each) to the following:

  1. Describe a trip you booked that went wrong and how you fixed it.
  2. You receive a bank compliance request with a 48-hour deadline and the founder is on a long-haul flight. What do you do?
  3. Have you managed personal or household matters, not just business, for a principal before? Give an example.
  4. Describe one repetitive task you automated for yourself or a previous principal: what the task was, which tools you used, and how much time it saved.
  5. What time zone are you in, and what hours are you realistically available?

Shortlisted candidates complete a 30-minute practical task (plan a sample trip from a short brief) before a video interview.

To apply: https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/ace-ventures-executive-personal-assistant-to-the-founder-remote-uae-or-europe

jobs.title: AssemblyAI: Senior Research Engineer
jobs.description:
Headquarters: Remote

Why AssemblyAI

AssemblyAI builds the best-in-class Voice AI models powering the next generation of voice applications. Our models serve 600M+ inference calls monthly, process 1M+ hours of audio daily, and power 2 billion+ end-user experiences. The Voice AI space is at an inflection point; we’re looking for folks truly excited to join a small team and help define the future of the industry.

We are one of the most capital-efficient AI companies on the planet - with under 100 people generating roughly $600K ARR per employee, we sit among the top 5 most revenue-dense teams within the fastest-growing AI companies today. That's not an accident; it's a deliberate choice to stay lean, move fast, and give every person on the team outsized ownership and impact. With thousands of customers including Granola, Fireflies, Figure AI, and CallRail, the company has real scale - processing over 2 million hours of audio daily and handling more than 1 million API calls every day. This is a rare growth-stage opportunity where the business is proven and the trajectory is steep, but the team is still small enough that your fingerprints are on everything.

If you've ever felt buried under layers of bureaucracy, starved of real ownership, or frustrated watching your work disappear into a slow-moving org, AssemblyAI is built differently. The company operates as a true meritocracy, with no heavy planning or approval processes and no gatekeeping on the tools or information you need. For anyone who genuinely cares about voice AI, not as a trend to chase, but as a technology to build,  this is the place where the most interesting problems at the most interesting scale are being solved by a team small enough that you'll actually know everyone's name.

We’re committed to creating a space where our employees can bring their full selves to work and have equal opportunity to succeed. No matter your race, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, religion, origin, ability, age, veteran status, if joining this mission speaks to you, we encourage you to apply!

About the Role

We're looking for a Senior Research Engineer to join our Research team, developing and improving the systems behind large-scale distributed training, data processing, and inference. Our goal as an organization is to solve customer problems and improve our products quickly through model development and measurement — and how fast we move depends on how quickly anyone here can run an experiment, measure it, and find out what's wrong. Raising that ceiling is the heart of this role. You'll be working inside the pipeline you're improving, not alongside it.

The ideal candidate has a deep understanding of modern deep learning systems, combined with strong engineering expertise across JAX and TPUs, layer-level optimization, large-scale distributed training, streaming, low-latency and asynchronous inference, inference compilers, and advanced parallelization techniques.

This is a cross-functional role. You'll work closely with our researchers, our infrastructure team, and production engineering — not as a handoff point, but as the person who learns enough of each domain to follow problems through to resolution. At times you'll train models, run evaluations, and analyze data yourself, both to deliver impact directly and to learn what's worth building to multiply the team's work. The bar is someone who understands the end-to-end impact they intend to make, measures it from the outset, and would rather find out they were wrong in a week than in a quarter. That discipline is what turns cross-functional ownership into an advantage.

The role is embedded within the Research team. 

What You’ll Do

  • Raise the team's experimental velocity — make it faster to launch an experiment job, get a number back you can trust, and know what to try next.
  • Maintain and evolve our JAX training framework, keeping it scalable and efficient for large-scale distributed training runs on TPU.
  • Improve the data our models learn from: investigating quality issues, building the tooling to surface them, and turning what you find into measurable accuracy gains.
  • Analyze the accuracy of production models, build evaluation harnesses, and work out which improvements will matter most to customers.
  • Translate research prototypes into production-ready systems, refactoring and modernizing model architectures and infrastructure along the way.
  • Optimize production inference for speech language models, both from a serving architecture perspective and through advanced techniques such as quantization and speculative decoding.
  • Investigate and resolve performance bottlenecks across the stack, from low-level kernels (XLA, Pallas) to high-level system design.
  • Partner with researchers, infrastructure, and production engineering to trace problems to their real source and ship fixes that hold.

What You’ll Need

  • Expert-level proficiency with JAX and TPUs, including the surrounding ecosystem (Flax, Optax, the XLA compilation pipeline).
  • Measurement discipline. You define what success looks like before you start, you stay skeptical of your own results until they hold up, and you treat an unexplained improvement as a problem rather than a win.
  • Appetite for the whole pipeline. Your core strength might be JAX and TPU performance, but when a customer issue traces back to a data problem or an evaluation blind spot, you want to go find it yourself. The people who do well here went deep in one area first, then kept expanding outward.
  • Strong experience optimizing inference systems for production, ideally with LLMs or speech models.
  • Deep understanding of distributed training at scale, modern deep learning systems, and ML infrastructure best practices.
  • Familiarity with modern inference optimization techniques: continuous batching, KV-cache management, sharding strategies, quantization.
  • Enthusiasm for refactoring and improving existing systems — you thrive on making products and code faster and better.
  • Strong Python skills; C++ or Rust experience for kernel-level work is a plus.
  • Excellent communication and a collaborative mindset — you can clearly explain complex tradeoffs and prioritize high-impact work.

Bonus

  • Domain knowledge in Speech-to-Text: ASR architectures, audio processing, streaming inference. 

Pay Transparency:

AssemblyAI strives to recruit and retain exceptional talent from diverse backgrounds while ensuring pay equity for our team. Our salary ranges are based on paying competitively for our size, stage, and industry, and are one part of many compensation, benefit, and other reward opportunities we provide.

There are many factors that go into salary determinations, including relevant experience, skill level, qualifications assessed during the interview process, and maintaining internal equity with peers on the team. The range shared below is a general expectation for the function as posted, but we are also open to considering candidates who may be more or less experienced than outlined in the job description. In this case, we will communicate any updates in the expected salary range.

The provided range is the expected salary for candidates in the U.S. Outside of those regions, there may be a change in the range which will be communicated to candidates throughout the interview process.

Salary range: $270,000 - $310,000

If you’re selected for an interview, please review this resource to better understand how AssemblyAI approaches the use of AI in our interview process.

Most of what a sales ops team used to do by hand is now something you can write software to do. Finding every company building voice AI before they contact us. Researching an account and drafting the first email. Watching product usage and telling an AE when a customer is about to expand or churn. Keeping the CRM clean without anyone filling in forms. You will build those systems, run them in production, and be judged on whether pipeline and revenue move.

Your users are our AEs, SDRs, and GTM leaders. Your job is to make a small team perform like one three times its size.

What You'll Do

  • Write code every day. Python services, SQL models, scheduled jobs, and small internal apps are most of the job. You'll use Claude Code and similar tools to ship in days what used to take a quarter.
  • Build agents that do the work: account research, lead qualification, outreach drafting, CRM hygiene, and usage monitoring. Design them, give them tools and data, evaluate their output, and keep them running.
  • Turn product usage data in BigQuery and Looker into signals sellers act on: usage alerts, expansion triggers, and account health scores.
  • Build the account targeting machine: sourcing, enrichment, dedupe, and ICP scoring, from raw data to a ranked list in a rep's queue.
  • Integrate the systems the team already uses (our CRM, enrichment providers, outbound tools) so data moves between them without a human in the loop.
  • Keep funnel data trustworthy: routing rules, field governance, and attribution.
  • Prototype fast, measure what works, kill what doesn't, and work directly with Sales and Marketing leadership on what to build next.
  • Document what you build so it keeps running without you.

What You'll Need

  • 4+ years as a software engineer, data engineer, or growth/GTM engineer, with time spent shipping systems that other people depend on.
  • Strong Python and SQL. You have owned production automations end to end: APIs, webhooks, scheduled jobs, retries, error handling, and monitoring.
  • Experience building with LLMs beyond a single prompt: multi-step agents, tool use, retrieval, and evaluation. You can tell whether an agent's output is good, and you know when a plain script is the better tool.
  • AI-assisted development is how you work. You use Claude Code or similar tools daily, and you have the engineering judgment to review, test, and stand behind what they produce.
  • Solid fundamentals: clean code, version control, code review, debugging, and a habit of thinking in systems. You do not need an engineering team to ship.
  • Curiosity about how a sales org works. You don't need a RevOps background, but you need to care about how deals get found and closed, and be willing to learn our CRM and the tools around it quickly.
  • A builder's mindset with an operator's judgment: you scope for business impact, ship iteratively, and measure results in pipeline and revenue.
  • Low ego, high ownership, and comfort being the single-threaded owner of an entire domain.

Nice to Have

  • Hands-on Salesforce or other CRM work at the object and API level, or experience with enrichment and outbound tools like Clay.
  • dbt, BigQuery, and Looker, or an equivalent warehouse and BI stack.
  • Time at a developer-facing or API-first company, or selling to technical buyers.
  • You've been the first engineer in a sales or growth org and built the function from scratch.

At Faire, we're using the power of tech, data, and machine learning to connect this thriving community of entrepreneurs across the globe. Picture your favorite boutique in town — we help them discover the best products from around the world to sell in their stores. With the right tools and insights, we believe that we can level the playing field so businesses can grow and local communities can thrive.

We’re looking for smart, resourceful and passionate people to join us as we power the shop local movement. If you believe in community, come join ours.

About this role

Faire is revolutionizing wholesale and helping local retailers and their suppliers succeed in a technology-enabled era. As a Director, Global Equity, you will own and continue to evolve Faire’s global equity programs, building on an existing foundation while enhancing the structure, rigor, and scalability required to support public company readiness. You'll report to the CMO, with a planned transition to the VP of Growth Marketing as that function scales, and work closely with Marketing Operations, Data, Lifecycle, and Campaigns to make sure paid-acquired users don't just land, but convert and stick.   • Own budget planning, pacing, and ROI reporting for all paid spend, and make the case for where to double down or pull back.

  • Build the measurement framework for CAC, signup/pipeline contribution, and payback by channel.
  • Partner with Lifecycle and Campaigns to make sure paid-acquired users flow into the right onboarding and activation journeys, not just land and drop off.
  • As the program proves out, build the roadmap and case for a fully staffed paid/performance team.

At Tines, our Customer Experience organization is recognized by customers for the quality of our work, responsiveness to their needs, and commitment to helping them realize meaningful value from our platform.

You will be accountable for renewal performance, forecasting accuracy, commercial execution, team development, and the processes that allow the function to scale.

You will also play a key role in strengthening the broader customer lifecycle at Tines, helping establish clear ownership and operating rhythms between Customer Success, Renewals, and Sales while ensuring that customer value, risk, and commercial strategy come together effectively at renewal.

  • Lead and develop a team of Renewal Managers, providing coaching, commercial guidance, and clear direction to drive strong customer and business outcomes.
  • Own renewal performance across the portfolio, with accountability for Gross Revenue Retention, renewal rate, churn and contraction outcomes, and on-time renewal execution.
  • Establish and maintain a consistent renewal forecast, providing leadership with clear visibility into renewal timing, risk, expected outcomes, and areas requiring intervention.
  • Guide Renewal Managers through complex customer negotiations involving pricing, contract terms, multi-year agreements, competitive pressure, procurement, and other commercial challenges.
  • Ensure renewal engagement begins early and that Renewal Managers have the customer context, risk signals, value realization, and relationship insights required to execute effectively.
  • Partner closely with Customer Success to ensure clear ownership between customer outcomes and commercial renewal execution, with CSMs focused on value, adoption, relationships, and risk mitigation while Renewals leads the commercial renewal process.
  • Collaborate with Sales and Account Management to identify and coordinate expansion opportunities associated with renewal cycles while maintaining clear ownership across teams.
  • Partner with Revenue Operations to improve renewal forecasting, CRM workflows, dashboards, automation, reporting, and operational discipline.
  • Develop scalable renewal motions across customer segments, including high-touch, mid-touch, and digital or automated approaches where appropriate.
  • Establish clear renewal playbooks, timelines, escalation paths, handoffs, and operating cadences that create consistency for customers and internal teams.
  • Establish and manage metrics and KPIs that measure renewal effectiveness, including GRR, logo retention, forecast accuracy, renewal timing, cycle time, multi-year adoption, team productivity, and portfolio health.
  • Recruit, onboard, develop, and retain strong commercial talent as the Renewals function and company continue to scale.

What will you bring with you?

  • 7+ years of experience in SaaS, enterprise software, Customer Success, Account Management, Renewals, Sales, or a similar commercial customer-facing environment.
  • 3+ years of people leadership experience, with a demonstrated track record of coaching and developing high-performing customer-facing or commercial teams.
  • Experience owning or managing a meaningful recurring revenue portfolio and delivering against retention or renewal targets.
  • A strong understanding of SaaS business metrics including ARR, Gross Revenue Retention, Net Revenue Retention, churn, contraction, renewal rate, and expansion.
  • Experience building and managing renewal forecasts with a high degree of operational rigor and predictability.
  • Strong commercial judgment and experience navigating pricing, negotiation, procurement, contracting, and customer objections.
  • The ability to coach teams through complex commercial situations while balancing customer relationships, revenue protection, and long-term business value.
  • Experience working closely with Customer Success and Sales teams to coordinate customer strategy and commercial outcomes.
  • Strong analytical skills and the ability to use data to identify trends, diagnose performance, and determine where intervention is required.
  • A track record of improving workflows, standardization, automation, or systems to increase organizational efficiency and capacity.
  • Strong cross-functional leadership skills and demonstrated ability to influence Revenue Operations, Sales, Customer Success, Finance, Legal, and executive stakeholders.
  • Excellent communication skills, with the ability to navigate both detailed commercial discussions and senior executive conversations.

What success looks like

In this role, you will build a Renewals organization that creates greater predictability for the business and a simpler, more consistent experience for customers.

Your team will engage customers earlier, identify and address risk before renewals become reactive, execute commercial conversations with confidence, and provide accurate visibility into renewal outcomes. Customer Success teams will be able to remain focused on driving value, adoption, strategic relationships, and risk mitigation while Renewal Managers bring dedicated commercial expertise to the renewal process.

At the same time, you will help Tines develop a renewal motion that can scale with the business combining strong talent, clear ownership, operational discipline, automation, and data to improve retention and strengthen long-term customer relationships.

jobs.title: Instacart: AI Solutions Lead, Marketing
jobs.description:
Headquarters: Canada - Remote (ON, AB, BC, or NS Only)

We're transforming the grocery industry

At Instacart, we invite the world to share love through food because we believe everyone should have access to the food they love and more time to enjoy it together. Where others see a simple need for grocery delivery, we see exciting complexity and endless opportunity to serve the varied needs of our community. We work to deliver an essential service that customers rely on to get their groceries and household goods, while also offering safe and flexible earnings opportunities to Instacart Personal Shoppers.

Instacart has become a lifeline for millions of people, and we’re building the team to help push our shopping cart forward. If you’re ready to do the best work of your life, come join our table.

Instacart is a Flex First team

There’s no one-size fits all approach to how we do our best work. Our employees have the flexibility to choose where they do their best work—whether it’s from home, an office, or your favorite coffee shop—while staying connected and building community through regular in-person events. Learn more about our flexible approach to where we work.

Why this role is on the menu

Most companies are layering AI onto existing processes. This role is about something different: rebuilding those processes from the ground up, so teams can do work that actually matters.

Instacart's Marketing team has set ambitious AI goals — and this is the person who makes them real. You'll be the first role of this kind in Marketing, embedded in the org with a clear mandate: identify what's slow, manual, or broken across the Marketing organization and rebuild it into something fundamentally better. The benchmark isn't marginal improvement. It's transformation — building solutions that make people wonder how they ever worked without them.

This is a builder role. Strategy is a means to an end. The end is something shipped, adopted, and measurable. You'll also be the connective tissue for Marketing's AI ambitions — convening the people who own AI goals, unblocking what's stuck, and creating internal momentum that makes the whole org move faster.

 

What you'll cook up in your first year

Building (60%)

  • Identify high-impact workflows, systems, and processes across Marketing that are slow, manual, or duct-taped together — and rebuild them AI-natively, from the ground up
  • Own the full cycle: understand the current state, design the solution, build it, ship it — then measure what changed. Establish the before, prove the after, and make the case to leadership
  • Walk in with work already queued. Early builds include:
    • Recurring leadership and planning narratives — transforming how Marketing produces its MBR, quarterly planning summaries, budget variance write-ups, and channel performance narratives; currently manual synthesis across multiple inputs, rebuilt into a faster, more consistent, AI-native output
    • Integrated campaign launch process — automating key steps from campaign ideation to launch, reducing the manual handoffs and coordination overhead that slow campaigns down across teams
    • Brief quality and standardization — an AI review layer that evaluates briefs before they leave the building, flags what's missing or unclear, and raises input quality across the org before downstream teams absorb the cost of a bad brief
  • Build with portability in mind — your solutions should be constructed so others can pick them up, adapt them for their own context, and extend what you've built without starting from scratch; you're not just solving a problem, you're creating infrastructure others can build on
  • Develop and maintain an intake framework: gather inputs from across the org, evaluate feasibility and impact, and make a defensible call on what gets built next — including what doesn't; prioritization discipline means saying no to low-value requests as readily as yes to high-value ones

Driving Adoption (20%)

  • Own the change management side of every build: create the conditions for people to trust what you've built, use it consistently, and not revert to old habits when something feels unfamiliar
  • Evangelize internally — write up wins, build case studies, show other teams what's possible; your goal is to generate more demand than you can supply, which means the org needs to see what AI can actually do, not just hear about it
  • Create energy around AI across Marketing — not as a cheerleader, but as someone who shows people things they didn't know were possible and makes it easy for them to take the next step

Orchestration & Thought Partnership (20%)

  • Lead the MarComms AI KR forum: convene AI KR owners across Marketing, create momentum behind shared goals, surface blockers, and hold the operating cadence
  • Act as a working partner to AI goal owners — unblocking vendor delays, solving capability gaps, helping people get unstuck

 

The secret ingredients we're looking for

Must-have pantry staples (Minimum Qualifications)

  • 7+ years in marketing operations, marketing strategy, or a closely adjacent discipline — you understand how marketing orgs work, where the friction lives, and what it costs to leave it unfixed
  • Proven builder with a track record of impact — you have shipped AI-powered workflows and processes that demonstrably changed how teams work; you can name the problem, describe the solution, and quantify the result.  You’re so invested in AI that you’ve applied it beyond the scope of your current role.
  • Hands-on daily experience with frontier AI tools such as Claude, GPT-4o, or Gemini, including writing prompts that produce reliable, production-quality output at scale
  • Experience building agentic systems where AI components interact with each other, including multi-agent design, orchestration layers, and workflows that run without a human in the loop at every step
  • An adoption-minded approach to building: designing for adoption from day one and taking accountability for whether what you built actually gets used
  • Strong communication skills, with the ability to explain what you're building, why it matters, and where it stands, for audiences from ICs to CMO-level leadership
  • Prioritization discipline — you can evaluate a request and tell someone their problem isn't a good AI candidate right now, or that the cost of building outstrips the benefit; you know what not to build

 

Optional garnishes (Preferred Qualifications)

  • A framework for evaluating AI vendors and tools quickly, including running comparison pilots and making principled decisions about what earns a place in the stack

Instacart provides highly market-competitive compensation and benefits in each location where our employees work.
